You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
A worker earns $40 per hour. Rather than work, she decides to visit a museum for three hours. The visit costs a total of $40. What is the opportunity cost of visiting the museum?
A newspaper article contains the following comments.
Which change in the way resources are allocated in an economy is consistent with moving from a planned economy to a market economy?

options.A: A minimum price guarantee for apple producers is removed.
options.B: A new government authority is established to monitor inefficiencies in apple production.
options.C: The production of apples is subsidised to increase output.
options.D: The sale of apples has a maximum price imposed.

questions.questionText: In which circumstance will the total expenditure by consumers on a good increase when its price increases?

options.A: Demand for the good is income elastic.
options.B: Demand for the good is price inelastic.
options.C: The price of a complementary good also increases.
options.D: The price of substitute goods also increases.

questions.questionText: When will a manufacturer’s ability to increase the quantity supplied in the short run be greater?

options.A: when labour is immobile
options.C: when the product is perishable
options.D: when unemployment is low

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for strawberries. The original equilibrium position is X. What will be the new position following the failure of strawberries to ripen and a fall in the price of cream (a complement to strawberries)? S price 3 S A S X B D D

options.C: 2 D D O quantity

questions.questionText: Good X is related to good Y. Incomes increase and the price of good Y falls. Which combination would give the greatest increase in demand for good X? relationship between nature of good X good X and good Y

options.A: inferior good complements
options.C: normal good complements
options.D: normal good substitutes

questions.questionText: What must be correct when the free market for a good is in disequilibrium?

options.A: Consumers can buy all of the good that they demand at the market price.
options.B: Producers can sell all of the good that they supply at the market price.
options.C: The market price of the good will not change.
options.D: The quantity of the good demanded differs from the quantity supplied.

questions.questionText: A power station burns waste to produce electricity. This also produces a by-product of fertiliser for farmers. What is the effect in the fertiliser market of an increase in the demand for electricity?

options.A: The price of fertiliser falls and the quantity demanded rises.
options.B: The price of fertiliser falls and the quantity supplied falls.
options.C: The price of fertiliser rises and the quantity demanded falls.
options.D: The price of fertiliser rises and the quantity supplied rises.

questions.questionText: The table shows the supply and demand for avocados in Mexico City. price per quantity demanded quantity supplied kilogram ($) per day (kg) per day (kg) 45 170 230 40 190 190 35 210 150
230 110 As a result of lower transport costs, supply rises by 60kg at all prices. What is the new equilibrium price?

The diagram shows a demand curve for pineapples. price X ($) 1.5 Y 0.5 D 0 3 6 9 12 quantity (000s) What happens to the value of price elasticity of demand (PED) when there is a movement from point X to point Y and what describes the value at point Y? effect on value of value of PED PED at Y

options.A: fall elastic
options.C: rise elastic
options.D: unchanged unitary

questions.questionText: Four firms produce furniture. The table shows the price elasticity of supply (PES) for each firm. If the price of furniture rises by 5% which firm would experience an increase in quantity supplied of 2.5%? PES for firm furniture
Which argument has often been used to justify the privatisation of state enterprises?

options.A: Private firms can produce the same outputs using fewer inputs.
options.B: Private firms try to earn large profits.
options.C: State enterprises are always monopolies which exploit consumers.
options.D: State enterprises cannot operate without government subsidies.

questions.questionText: A government imposes a maximum rent in order to make rented housing more affordable. What is likely to be a long-run consequence if the maximum is set below the current free market level?

options.A: a shortage of applicants for rented housing
options.C: an increase in supply to satisfy the increased demand for rented housing
options.D: an increase in the number of houses being rented

questions.questionText: What would be categorised as direct government provision of goods and services?

options.A: a government grant to a firm to provide healthcare services
options.B: a government regulation on the amount of sugar in soft drinks
options.C: a government subsidy to a firm that operates a regional train service
options.D: a government takeover of a local bus service

questions.questionText: Which type of tax is the 15% sales tax levied in South Africa?

options.A: ad valorem direct
options.C: specific direct
options.D: specific indirect

questions.questionText: What is an example of a transfer payment?

options.A: a household moving savings from one bank account to another
options.B: a monthly repayment on a loan used to buy a new cooker
options.C: the amount paid to transport goods from one city to another
options.D: the payment of student grants by the government

questions.questionText: What will lead to an immediate improvement in the balance of payments deficit on current account?

options.A: a fall in interest rates
options.B: a reduction in dividend payments to foreign investors
options.C: a reduction in the standard rate of income tax
options.D: an increase in the level of government current expenditure

questions.questionText: An appreciation of the South African rand in the foreign exchange markets is most likely to assist the South African government achieve which policy objective?

options.A: a redistribution of income
options.B: a reduction in the rate of inflation
options.C: a reduction in the volume of imports
options.D: an increase in the level of employment

questions.questionText: Four countries, A, B, C and D, trade internationally. Each circle in the diagram represents a free trade area between the countries within the circle. A country can belong to more than one free trade area. Countries outside of a circle face trade barriers. Which country has the greatest opportunity to benefit from free international trade? A C B D
The diagram shows Greece’s trade position with the EU between 2005 and 2014. Greek trade key $bn 40 imports from EU

A central bank forecasts a rise in raw material costs. The government plans to increase spending on health and education. The initial equilibrium point is shown by X on the aggregate demand, AD, and aggregate supply, AS, diagram. What would be the new equilibrium point in the short run if the forecasts prove to be accurate and the government plans are implemented? AS general AS AS price C 2 level

options.D: X B A AD AD AD 2 O real output

questions.questionText: A country with a floating exchange rate experiences a large surplus on the current account of its balance of payments. What is likely to decrease as a consequence?

options.A: exports of capital from the country
options.B: the level of employment in the county
options.C: the prices of imports into the country
options.D: the value of the country’s currency

questions.questionText: In 2018 an investor in the United States (US) purchased shares in a German bank. In December 2018 the US investor was paid a dividend on these shares. How were these activities recorded in the US balance of payments for 2018? share purchase dividend payment

options.A: capital account credit current account credit
options.B: capital account credit current account debit
options.C: capital account debit current account credit
options.D: capital account debit current account debit

questions.questionText: Which statement describes disinflation?

options.A: a fall in the price level
options.B: a fall in the rate of inflation
options.C: a rise in the value of money
options.D: inflation below zero

questions.questionText: In a closed economy a rise in aggregate demand is needed to increase output in the country. What is necessary to achieve this increase in output in the economy?

options.A: enough capacity to produce the extra goods and services demanded
options.B: free trade to allow imports to make up any shortages in supply
options.C: government spending to be less than tax revenue
options.D: reduced credit to lower inflation

questions.questionText: A country with a fixed exchange rate and a deficit in the current account of its balance of payments enters a recession. It devalues its currency in an effort to correct its balance of payments. Under which conditions is the deficit most likely to improve? price elasticity of price elasticity of income elasticity of demand for imports demand for exports demand for imports
What is an example of fiscal policy aimed at increasing aggregate demand in an economy?

options.A: increasing expenditure by firms on skills training programmes for unskilled workers
options.B: increasing the commercial banks’ lending ability
options.C: reducing the rate of income tax for all income earners
options.D: reducing the rate of interest on loans to manufacturing companies
